key_insight: Putting trainable nonlinear functions on physical connections, rather than using devices only as scalar weights, makes analogue neural networks much better at learning smooth continuous targets.
engineering_relevance: This enables low-power hardware control systems and solar maximum-power-point tracking with far fewer nodes and connections, while remaining compatible with CMOS, field-programmable analogue arrays, and memristive implementations.
method: Implemented trainable nonlinear connection functions as analogue band-pass filters on field-programmable analogue arrays
Trained physical networks on smooth regression/control tasks such as robotic kinematics, continuous control, and photovoltaic maximum-power-point tracking
Compared representational efficiency against multilayer perceptrons and tested hardware transfer across ~35,000 connections
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the approach achieves far fewer nodes and connections on smooth tasks, but shows no parameter-efficiency advantage on classification-like decision boundaries, with transfer fidelity quantified across approximately 35,000 connections.
watch_item: The benefit is task-dependent, so this architecture may not improve efficiency for classification-style problems or nonsmooth decision boundaries.
paper_title: Low-power analogue neural networks with trainable nonlinear connections for continuous control
